blindSummary:
A parliamentary inquiry by this state/province's legislature documents that queer-hostile offences recorded by police rose from 33 in 2022 to 83 in 2023 - a 150 % jump in two years in one state/province. The assessment flags an irreducible ambiguity: the increase may reflect a real deterioration in safety or a change in police classification practices under a newer national police reporting category for LGBTQ crimes. No state/province-specific trans statute, ordinance or documented event-attack series was found here beyond this statistical finding.

The local deviation is a minimal negative one against the country-wide average, treating the trend as a mild negative climate indicator whose causality is unresolved. Unlike a neighbouring state/province, this one has no legislative hostility of any kind - it joined no initiative against the national self-identification law and imposed no administrative-language ban - and the statistical signal is the only differentiator, and it is caveated.
